groups.heading: Reminder about Exercise 7, Task 3.2
paragraphs: In the coming exercises, you will also compare [the protocols] by *measurement*, with respect to their **performance**. points: the **latency** from launching an auction until a bid arrives
the number of **auctions or bids per second** an auction house sustains

slides.title: About the Exercise: What You Know So Far
slides.alt: Deployment diagram with Client, Auctioneer, an EventQueue, a PITAS application with Bidder, pitas-jobs and pitas-scheduler, and pitas-worker-pool, and a Worker. No pods and no interactions are shown yet.

slides.title: About the Exercise: Setup and Commission
slides.alt: Deployment diagram with Client, ClientPod, Auctioneer, an EventQueue, an AuctionHousePods group with AuctioneerPod and BidderPod, a PITAS application with Bidder, pitas-jobs and pitas-scheduler, and pitas-worker-pool, and a Worker with WorkerPod. Steps 1 to 8 show, in green: the Worker registers its WebID with pitas-worker-pool, writes its details to WorkerPod, and the pool stores the WebID in BidderPod. The Client writes the task input to ClientPod and commissions the task with a link. The Auctioneer creates the auction in AuctioneerPod and pushes an auction event, which the EventQueue delivers to the Bidder.
slides.notes: This flow is one example of how the sovereignty rules can work. Your implementation can differ from it.

slides.title: About the Exercise: Bidding and Award
slides.alt: Deployment diagram with Client, ClientPod, Auctioneer, an EventQueue, an AuctionHousePods group with AuctioneerPod and BidderPod, a PITAS application with Bidder, pitas-jobs and pitas-scheduler, and pitas-worker-pool, and a Worker with WorkerPod. Steps 1 to 8 show in black. Steps 9 to 16 show in green: the Bidder reads the auction, fetches the registered Worker WebIDs and the worker details from WorkerPod, evaluates the auction and appends a bid to AuctioneerPod. The Auctioneer reads the bids, evaluates them and writes the award.
slides.notes: This flow is one example of how the sovereignty rules can work. Your implementation can differ from it.

slides.title: About the Exercise: Award and Execution
slides.alt: Deployment diagram with Client, ClientPod, Auctioneer, an EventQueue, an AuctionHousePods group with AuctioneerPod and BidderPod, a PITAS application with Bidder, pitas-jobs and pitas-scheduler, and pitas-worker-pool, and a Worker with WorkerPod. Steps 1 to 16 show in black. Steps 17 to 23 show in green: the Auctioneer pushes an award event, the EventQueue delivers it, the Bidder reads the award and hands the won job over to pitas-jobs, which dispatches it to the Worker. The Worker fetches the task input from ClientPod and executes it without keeping a copy.
slides.notes: This flow is one example of how the sovereignty rules can work. Your implementation can differ from it.

slides.title: About the Exercise: Result Back to the Client
slides.alt: Deployment diagram with Client, ClientPod, Auctioneer, an EventQueue, an AuctionHousePods group with AuctioneerPod and BidderPod, a PITAS application with Bidder, pitas-jobs and pitas-scheduler, and pitas-worker-pool, and a Worker with WorkerPod. Steps 1 to 23 show in black. Steps 24 to 30 show in green: the Worker appends the result to ClientPod and reports execution done, the Bidder polls the job status and pushes a result event, the EventQueue delivers it to the Auctioneer, which notifies the Client with a link, and the Client reads the result from ClientPod.
slides.notes: This flow is one example of how the sovereignty rules can work. Your implementation can differ from it.
